name: Texas
requirementsNote: Texas state law does not mandate renters insurance, but property managers frequently require proof of coverage in standard rental agreements.
seoDescription: Estimate renters insurance costs in Texas based on personal property, liability limits, and deductible options.

demographics.demographicNote: Most Texas renters choose thirty thousand dollars in personal property coverage with a five hundred dollar deductible, though renters in Austin and Dallas often increase this to twenty five thousand to forty thousand dollars given the state's rising cost of living.

riskFactors.title: Highest Tornado Count in the Nation
riskFactors.description: Texas recorded one hundred sixty nine confirmed tornadoes in 2024, more than any other state, and the state has averaged well over one hundred tornadoes a year for the past decade. Wind and tornado damage to personal belongings is covered under a standard Texas renters insurance policy.

riskFactors.title: Gulf Coast Hurricanes
riskFactors.description: Hurricane Harvey dumped over sixty inches of rain on Houston in 2017, causing catastrophic flooding, and Hurricane Beryl generated over twenty two thousand wind damage claims through the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association in a single event in 2024. Wind damage from a hurricane is covered under a standard renters policy, though flooding is not.

riskFactors.title: North Texas Hail and Hill Country Flash Flooding
riskFactors.description: North Texas hailstorms caused a record five billion dollars in homeowner losses in 2016 alone, including the costliest single hailstorm in state history in San Antonio. The Texas Hill Country separately faces persistent, deadly flash flood risk from intense rainfall. Hail is covered under standard renters insurance, while flash flood damage is excluded and requires a separate policy.

faqs.question: Is renters insurance required in Texas?
faqs.answer: No. Texas law does not require renters insurance, but most landlords and apartment complexes include coverage requirements in lease agreements.

faqs.question: Does renters insurance cover hurricane damage in Texas?
faqs.answer: Wind damage from a hurricane is generally covered, but flooding from rain or storm surge is essentially never covered by renters insurance. This is critical for Gulf Coast renters in Houston, Galveston, or Corpus Christi.

faqs.question: Does renters insurance cover tornado damage in Texas?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tornado winds and hail are covered by a standard Texas renters insurance policy, relevant statewide given Texas recorded more tornadoes than any other state in 2024.

faqs.question: Does renters insurance cover hail damage in North Texas?
faqs.answer: Yes. Hail damage to personal belongings is covered under a standard renters policy, which matters significantly in North Texas, where hailstorms caused a record five billion dollars in losses in a single year.

faqs.question: How much does renters insurance cost in Texas?
faqs.answer: Texas renters insurance runs above the national average, with Houston and coastal areas costing more due to hurricane exposure while inland cities like San Antonio and Arlington tend to be more affordable. blogContent.whyThisRate: Texas renters insurance costs rank above the national average because the state genuinely faces every major weather risk category at once. Texas led the nation with one hundred sixty nine confirmed tornadoes in 2024, spread across a state large enough to include Tornado Alley in the north, hurricane exposed Gulf Coast cities like Houston and Corpus Christi, and severe hail corridors across North Texas. Hurricane Harvey's sixty inches of rain over Houston in 2017 and Hurricane Beryl's twenty two thousand wind claims in 2024 illustrate the coastal risk, while a record five billion dollars in hail losses in a single 2016 season shows how costly North Texas storms can be independent of any hurricane. The Texas Hill Country adds a fourth, distinct hazard in deadly flash flooding driven by intense rainfall over limestone terrain. Because Texas spans such varied geography, few other states combine this many separate weather risks into one statewide rate.
blogContent.howCalculated: For a standard profile, twenty thousand dollars in personal property coverage, one hundred thousand dollars in liability, and a five hundred dollar deductible, our Texas renters insurance calculator applies the state's base rate of two hundred twenty dollars a year with no adjustment at these default levels, landing around one hundred ninety four to two hundred forty six dollars a year, or roughly sixteen to twenty one dollars a month. Renters near the Gulf Coast should confirm windstorm coverage through the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association if their standard policy excludes it, and budget separately for flood insurance given that flooding is essentially never covered by a standard renters policy.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Within the South region, Texas's rate sits below Louisiana and Florida despite carrying tornado, hurricane, and hail risk simultaneously, since no single hazard dominates the way hurricane risk does in those Gulf Coast states. Compared to the national average, Texas renters insurance runs meaningfully higher, reflecting the sheer breadth of weather risk the state's size and geography force insurers to price into every policy.
